subject.title: Control-plane hardening from Optimus ops findings

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this combined diagnose JSON, plugin-contract validator, and persistent diagnostic-state surface as one permanent operator contract?
rationale: The PR adds multiple public CLI and data contracts plus security-sensitive persistence behavior; code correctness alone cannot determine whether that combined product boundary should exist or be split.

options.title: Split and harden
options.body: Require narrower PRs for diagnose, plugin validation, provenance, and SQLite-backed diagnostic state, each with focused exact-head proof.

options.title: Approve combined contract
options.body: Accept the combined operator surface after the blocking storage and metric defects are fixed, the branch is rebased, and exact-head upgrade and redaction proof is supplied.

options.title: Decline the stack
options.body: Close the PR and retain only independently justified pieces through new narrowly scoped proposals.

recommendation.title: Split and harden
recommendation.body: Require narrower PRs for diagnose, plugin validation, provenance, and SQLite-backed diagnostic state, each with focused exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal covers the CLI, daemon audit, and plugin-manifest boundaries defining most of this operator contract.
